questions.question: You are driving a heavy goods vehicle (GVM over 3,500 kg) and come across a blue circular command sign displaying the symbol of a motor car at the entrance to a specific carriageway. What does this sign legally mandate?

options.text: The designated road or lane is reserved exclusively for motor cars; heavy goods vehicles, motorcycles, buses, and non-motorized vehicles are strictly prohibited from entering.
All vehicles may enter the roadway, but heavy vehicles must maintain a minimum distance of 50 meters behind any motor car ahead.
Motor cars must yield right-of-way to heavy vehicles when entering or exiting this roadway.

questions.question: You are driving a private passenger vehicle and approach a road or dedicated lane marked with a blue circular command sign showing a taxi symbol. Which statement accurately states your legal requirement?

options.text: You may use the taxi lane to bypass heavy traffic during peak hours, provided you do not stop or park.
The designated lane, roadway, or parking area is reserved strictly for authorized taxis; private vehicles and all other non-taxi traffic are legally prohibited from using it.
Private vehicles are allowed in the lane only if they are carrying three or more passengers (carpooling).

questions.question: You are driving a private motor car along a multi-lane urban street and see a blue circular command sign displaying the symbol of a minibus posted above the right-hand lane. What is your legal obligation regarding that lane?

options.text: Private vehicles may use the lane to overtake slower vehicles, provided they return to the left lane within 200 meters.
The designated lane is reserved exclusively for minibuses; all other vehicles, including private cars, trucks, and motorcycles, are strictly prohibited from driving in or using it.
All light passenger vehicles carrying 5 or more passengers are permitted to use the lane alongside minibuses.

questions.question: You are driving a standard motor car and approach a road or dedicated lane displaying a blue circular command sign showing the symbol of a midibus. What does this sign legally mandate?

options.text: Only midibuses are permitted to use that lane or road segment; other vehicles, including private motor cars, heavy trucks, and motorcycles, are strictly prohibited.
Midi-sized commercial delivery vans under 3,500 kg GVM may share the lane with midibuses during non-peak hours.
Private motor cars carrying 8 or more passengers are legally permitted to use the midibus lane.

questions.question: You are driving a private motor car along an urban roadway and notice a blue circular command sign displaying the symbol of a standard bus mounted over the left lane. What is your legal duty regarding this lane?

options.text: You may drive in the bus lane during off-peak hours, provided you vacate the lane as soon as a bus approaches from behind.
The lane is reserved exclusively for standard buses; all other vehicles, including private motor cars, minibuses, and delivery trucks, are strictly prohibited from using it.
Private motor cars carrying four or more passengers (high-occupancy vehicles) are legally permitted to use the bus lane.

questions.question: You are looking for parking near a shopping district and spot a dedicated bay/lane marked with a blue circular command sign displaying a delivery vehicle symbol. What is the legal requirement for using this space?

options.text: Private motor vehicles may park in the bay for up to 15 minutes while picking up or dropping off passengers.
The designated lane, bay, or roadway is reserved exclusively for goods vehicles actively loading or unloading goods; private passenger vehicles are strictly prohibited from using it.
Any vehicle under 3,500 kg GVM may park in the bay outside of normal business hours (after 18:00).

questions.question: You are driving a private passenger car and encounter a roadway or dedicated lane marked with a blue circular command sign displaying the symbol of a goods vehicle. What is your strict legal obligation?

options.text: You are strictly prohibited from driving in or entering that lane or roadway, as it is legally reserved exclusively for goods vehicles.
You may use the lane provided you do not exceed 60 km/h and do not block faster commercial trucks behind you.
You may enter the lane only between 18:00 and 06:00 when goods traffic is light.

questions.question: You are driving a light commercial vehicle with a Gross Vehicle Mass (GVM) of 3,500 kg (3.5 tonnes). You approach a multi-lane roadway displaying a blue circular command sign showing a truck symbol with "10t" inside. Which statement correctly describes your legal duty?

options.text: You must move into this lane immediately because all commercial goods vehicles regardless of weight are required to use it.
You are legally prohibited from using this designated lane or roadway because your vehicle's GVM does not exceed 10 tonnes.
You may use the designated lane only during night-time hours when heavy traffic is reduced.

questions.question: You are driving a private motor car near an active building site and encounter a blue circular command sign displaying the symbol of a construction vehicle at the entrance to a lane or access road. What does this sign legally mandate?

options.text: Private motor vehicles may enter the access road, provided they use hazard lights and yield right-of-way to all construction machinery.
Only designated construction vehicles and heavy site machinery are legally permitted to enter or use that lane/roadway; all other motor vehicles are strictly prohibited.
All vehicles driving through the area must maintain a minimum speed of 30 km/h to clear the construction zone quickly.

questions.question: You are driving a standard commercial truck and encounter a blue circular command sign displaying the symbol of an abnormal vehicle or load at the entrance to a specific bypass lane. What is your legal obligation?

options.text: Standard commercial trucks may use the lane if they carry a yellow flashing light, but private passenger cars are banned.
You are strictly prohibited from entering or using this lane, as it is legally reserved exclusively for vehicles with abnormal dimensions or loads.
All heavy vehicles weighing over 3,500 kg GVM are required to enter the lane regardless of whether their dimensions are abnormal.
